cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD. Ezekiel looks up and sees the likeness of a throne, and then the LORD speaks to the man clothed in linen. The words are a command: "Go inside the wheelwork beneath the cherubim." (Ezekiel 10:2) The LORD is the one giving the orders.

The answer is burning coals. The LORD says, "Fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim…" (Ezekiel 10:2) Burning coals, in your hands, friends. I work with ovens all day and even I say, wow.
The answer is True. The LORD says to fill his hands with burning coals and "…scatter them over the city." (Ezekiel 10:2) The coals have somewhere to go. They are meant for the city.

The answer is over the threshold of the temple. "Then the glory of the LORD rose from above the cherubim and stood over the threshold of the temple." (Ezekiel 10:4) The threshold is the doorway, the spot you cross to go in or out. The glory moves up and takes a stand right there.

The answer is False. Ezekiel says the temple was filled with the cloud, and "…the court was filled with the brightness of the glory of the LORD." (Ezekiel 10:4) Cloud and brightness together, friends. Darkness never makes the list.
The answer is voice. The sound of the wings is "…like the voice of God Almighty when He speaks." (Ezekiel 10:5) And that sound of the wings could be heard as far as the outer court.

The answer is one of the cherubim. "…one of the cherubim reached out his hand and took some of the fire that was among them." (Ezekiel 10:7) Then he put it into the hands of the man clothed in linen. The fire is handed over, not grabbed.
The answer is False. After the cherub puts the fire in his hands, the man clothed in linen "…received it and went out." (Ezekiel 10:7) He doesn't stay among the cherubim.
The answer is a beryl stone. "…the wheels gleamed like a beryl stone." (Ezekiel 10:9) Ezekiel picks a gem to describe the shine, friends. These wheels aren't dull, they're sparkling.

The answer is that they go straight without turning. Ezekiel says, "…they would go in any of the four directions, without turning as they moved." (Ezekiel 10:11) Four directions and no turning. Meanwhile I need three tries to get around my own counter.

The answer is True. The text says, "…wherever the head faced, the cherubim would go in that direction, without turning as they moved." (Ezekiel 10:11) Wherever the head faces, that's the direction they go. And they don't turn to do it.
The answer is wheels. The cherubim's bodies are full of eyes all around, "…as were their four wheels." (Ezekiel 10:12) The wheels aren't just along for the ride, friends. They get the eyes too.

The answer is a lion and an eagle. Ezekiel says each of the cherubim had four faces: "the first face was that of a cherub, the second that of a man, the third that of a lion, and the fourth that of an eagle." (Ezekiel 10:14) That's four faces on every one of them.
The answer is True. Ezekiel says, "These were the living creatures I had seen by the River Kebar." (Ezekiel 10:15) He had seen them before, at the River Kebar. This isn't his first time.

The answer is that the spirit of the creatures was in the wheels. The wheels did all that, "…for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels." (Ezekiel 10:17) The two move as one because the same spirit is in both. That's the reason the text gives, friends.

The answer is cherubim. "…the glory of the LORD moved away from the threshold of the temple and stood above the cherubim." (Ezekiel 10:18) It leaves the threshold and stands above them. Then the cherubim lift their wings and rise (Ezekiel 10:19).

The answer is the entrance of the east gate. The text says, "…they stopped at the entrance of the east gate of the house of the LORD, with the glory of the God of Israel above them." (Ezekiel 10:19) The glory of the God of Israel is above them as they stop. The wheels are beside them as they go.
The answer is False. Ezekiel says, "Each had four faces and four wings, with what looked like human hands under their wings." (Ezekiel 10:21) Four wings, friends, not six.
